items.stem: Explain the term “a primary amine”.
items.answer: An amine in which one hydrogen of ammonia is replaced by an alkyl or aryl group.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: an amine in which one hydrogen of ammonia is replaced by an alkyl or aryl group.

items.stem: Which structure corresponds to methanamine?
items.answer: CH₃NH₂
items.markingKey: (b) methanamine = CH₃NH₂.

CH₃NH₂
CH₃CH₂NHCH₃

items.stem:
Assertion (A): The C–N–H bond angle in amines is 120°.
Reason (R): Hoffmann bromamide degradation gives an amine with one carbon less than the amide.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A is false: Nitrogen is sp³; the angle is about 108° (pyramidal). R is a true statement.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “Hoffmann bromamide degradation gives an amine with the same number of carbons as the amide.”
items.answer: One carbon is lost (as carbonate).
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: One carbon is lost (as carbonate).

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Ammonolysis of alkyl halides gives a pure primary amine.
Reason (R): The primary amine formed can react further with alkyl halide.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A mixture of 1°, 2°, 3° amines and quaternary salt is obtained; the reason is true.

Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.

items.stem:
Harish has propanamide in his laboratory and wants ethanamine.
(i) Name the reaction he should use and give the reagents. (2 marks)
(ii) How many carbon atoms are lost? (1 mark)
(iii) Which reagent would convert propanamide into propan-1-amine instead? (1 mark)
items.answer: (i) Hoffmann bromamide degradation with Br₂ and aqueous NaOH. (ii) One carbon is lost (as Na₂CO₃). (iii) LiAlH₄ followed by H₂O.

items.stem: How is C₆H₅NHCH₃ classified?
items.answer: a secondary amine
items.markingKey: (c) A secondary amine: C₆H₅NHCH₃ has the nitrogen bonded to the number of carbon groups that defines a secondary amine.
options: a quaternary ammonium salt
a tertiary amine
a secondary amine
a primary amine

items.stem: In the Hoffmann bromamide degradation, 20.0 g of benzamide (C₆H₅CONH₂) is treated with Br₂ and aqueous NaOH. Identify the amine and calculate its mass if the yield is 60%. (Molar masses: amide 121, amine 93 g mol⁻¹)
items.answer: aniline (C₆H₅NH₂); 9.22 g
items.markingKey: RCONH₂ + Br₂ + 4NaOH → RNH₂ + Na₂CO₃ + 2NaBr + 2H₂O: one carbon is lost, giving aniline (1); n = 20.0/121 = 0.165 mol (1); mass = n × 93 × 60% = 9.22 g (1).

items.stem: What is the IUPAC name of C₆H₅CH₂NH₂?
items.answer: phenylmethanamine
items.markingKey: (c) C₆H₅CH₂NH₂ = phenylmethanamine.
options: N-methylbenzenamine
2-methylbenzenamine
phenylmethanamine
benzenamine

items.stem: Which term describes the preparation of primary aliphatic amines from phthalimide, KOH and an alkyl halide followed by hydrolysis?
items.answer: Gabriel phthalimide synthesis
items.markingKey: (b) Gabriel phthalimide synthesis: the preparation of primary aliphatic amines from phthalimide, KOH and an alkyl halide followed by hydrolysis.
options: Hoffmann bromamide degradation
Gabriel phthalimide synthesis
a quaternary ammonium salt
a primary amine

items.stem: Which of the following statements about structure, classification, nomenclature and preparation of amines is correct?
items.answer: Reduction of nitrobenzene with Fe and HCl is preferred industrially.
items.markingKey: (a) Reduction of nitrobenzene with Fe and HCl is preferred industrially. The other statements are false. Aryl halides do not undergo nucleophilic substitution with the phthalimide anion; it gives only 1° aliphatic amines. One carbon is lost (as carbonate). Nitrile reduction gives amines with the same carbon chain; the chain is one carbon longer than the alkyl halide used.
options: Reduction of nitrobenzene with Fe and HCl is preferred industrially.
Reduction of nitriles gives amines with one carbon less.
Hoffmann bromamide degradation gives an amine with the same number of carbons as the amide.
Gabriel phthalimide synthesis is used to prepare aniline.

items.stem: Why cannot aniline be prepared by Gabriel phthalimide synthesis? Suggest a method to prepare it.
items.answer: Aryl halides do not undergo nucleophilic substitution with the phthalimide anion. Aniline is made by reduction of nitrobenzene with Sn/HCl or Fe/HCl (or H₂/Pd).
items.markingKey: 1 mark reason; 1 mark method.

items.stem: Explain the term “a quaternary ammonium salt”.
items.answer: A salt R₄N⁺X⁻ in which all four hydrogens of the ammonium ion are replaced by alkyl groups.

Reduction of nitrobenzene with Fe and HCl is preferred industrially.

items.stem: What is meant by “a zwitterion”?
items.answer: A dipolar ion with both positive and negative charges, as in sulphanilic acid.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about physical properties, basicity and reactions of amines is correct?
items.answer: Aniline does not undergo Friedel–Crafts reaction.
items.markingKey: (c) Aniline does not undergo Friedel–Crafts reaction. The other statements are false. The lone pair of aniline is delocalised into the ring; it is much weaker (pKb 9.38 vs 3.38). A large amount of m-nitroaniline also forms because the anilinium ion is meta-directing. Only primary amines give it.
options: Secondary amines give the carbylamine test.
Aniline is a stronger base than methylamine.
Aniline does not undergo Friedel–Crafts reaction.
Nitration of aniline gives only p-nitroaniline.

less basic than ammonia

items.stem: Which of the following shows the correct order of basic strength in aqueous solution?
items.answer: (C₂H₅)₂NH > (C₂H₅)₃N > C₂H₅NH₂ > NH₃
items.markingKey: (C₂H₅)₂NH > (C₂H₅)₃N > C₂H₅NH₂ > NH₃. Combination of +I effect, solvation of the ammonium ion and steric effects.
options: (C₂H₅)₃N > NH₃ > C₂H₅NH₂ > (C₂H₅)₂NH
NH₃ > C₂H₅NH₂ > (C₂H₅)₃N > (C₂H₅)₂NH
(C₂H₅)₂NH > (C₂H₅)₃N > C₂H₅NH₂ > NH₃

items.stem:
Pooja nitrates aniline directly and gets a mixture with a lot of m-nitroaniline. She then acetylates aniline first.
(i) Why is much m-nitroaniline formed? (1 mark)
(ii) What does acetylation achieve? (2 marks)
(iii) Which product does she get after hydrolysis? (1 mark)
items.answer: (i) In strongly acidic medium aniline is protonated to the anilinium ion, which is meta-directing. (ii) The acetyl group reduces the activating effect (lone pair also shared with C=O), prevents protonation/oxidation and allows mono-nitration at para. (iii) p-Nitroaniline (major).

items.stem: Arrange (C₂H₅)₂NH, (C₂H₅)₃N, C₂H₅NH₂ and NH₃ in decreasing order of basic strength in water, and explain why the order is not simply 3° > 2° > 1°.
items.answer: (C₂H₅)₂NH > (C₂H₅)₃N > C₂H₅NH₂ > NH₃. Besides the +I effect, the solvation (H-bonding) of the ammonium ion and steric hindrance matter: 3° ammonium ions are poorly solvated.
items.markingKey: 1 mark order; 1 mark explanation.

items.answer: Benzenesulphonyl chloride reacts with 1° amines to give N-alkylbenzenesulphonamide, which has an acidic N–H and dissolves in alkali (C₆H₅SO₂Cl + C₂H₅NH₂ → C₆H₅SO₂NHC₂H₅). 2° amines give N,N-dialkylbenzenesulphonamide, insoluble in alkali (C₆H₅SO₂N(C₂H₅)₂). 3° amines do not react.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about diazonium salts is correct?
items.answer: Coupling of benzenediazonium chloride with phenol gives an orange dye.
items.markingKey: (b) Coupling of benzenediazonium chloride with phenol gives an orange dye. The other statements are false. It is carried out at 273–278 K because diazonium salts decompose at higher temperatures. They decompose at once giving N₂ and carbocations; only arenediazonium salts are fairly stable. Coupling occurs at the para position.
options: Diazotisation is carried out at about 350 K.
Coupling of benzenediazonium chloride with phenol gives an orange dye.
Alkyldiazonium salts are stable at room temperature.
Azo coupling with phenol occurs at the meta position.
